title: autotune-defaults: add smart batching/caching defaults, quantization profiles, and unit-econ reporting
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Our autotune pipeline needs a set of sensible defaults for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles so teams get immediate unit-econom improvements without manual tuning. This PR implements: 1) a new defaults engine that recommends batching and caching parameters based on traffic percentiles and model latency targets; 2) two curated quantization profiles (speed-first and quality-first) with runtime-aware compatibility checks; and 3) a unit-economics reporting pipeline that emits per-route per-model token cost estimates and cost-breakdown metrics for the console and Optimize tooling. Changes are backward compatible: defaults are opt-in for Dedicated/Private customers and opt-out via config for Hosted. Implementation notes: - Adds autotune/defaults service + REST API and CLI hooks. - Introduces quant-profiles YAMLs and a runtime compatibility checker (accepts model architecture + dtype + max_seq). - Pipeline integrates with existing metrics exporter to emit uecon.* namespaces and a new daily summary job that populates Optimize's model recommendations. - Adds end-to-end tests and integration tests for the compatibility checker. Checklist: - [x] Defaults engine with percentile-based recommendations - [x] Quantization profiles and safety checks - [x] Unit-econ metric emission and daily summarizer - [x] E2E tests + load tests - [x] Docs update (console + SDK notes) Rollout plan: staged rollout on staging for 48h with A/B traffic split, then enable for 10% of production routes, observe uecon metrics for 1 week, then expand. Rollback: toggle via feature flag; quant-profiles are non-destructive and require explicit apply. Related: ENG-4523 (autotune defaults), ENG-4590 (quant profiles), SUP-1021 (support request for inexplicable cost spikes).

review_comments: Marco Diaz: Overall looks solid. Two concerns: 1) the defaults engine could recommend too-large batch sizes for low-memory GPUs - can we cap by detected device_mem? 2) need a safety timeout when applying quant profiles to avoid long recompile pauses.
Aisha Patel: Good catches. Added device memory-aware cap to estimator and a 30s apply timeout with exponential backoff. See compat_checker.py changes and added tests for timeouts.
Sophie Chen: Metrics look good. Please add a tag to differentiate autotune-generated recommendations vs user overrides so Optimize can attribute savings.
Aisha Patel: Added "autotune_source" label to uecon metrics and included attribution in the daily summary output.
ci_checks: load-test-staging: pass (summary: 2% latency regression at p99 under 10k rps; within SLO)
release_notes: Added autotune defaults engine to recommend batching/caching settings out-of-the-box, two curated quantization profiles (speed-first, quality-first), and unit-economics metrics export for Optimize. Defaults are opt-in; see docs for rollout and opt-out instructions.
